```{r}
library(patchwork)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(boot)
```
```{r}
my_bootstrap <- function(data, stat_fn, B = 1000, conf = 0.95, seed = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)
  n <- nrow(data)

  # Step 1: Calculate the observed point estimate on the original sample
  theta_hat <- stat_fn(data)

  # Steps 2 & 3: Resample with replacement B times and calculate stat_fn
  boot_estimates <- numeric(B)

  for (b in 1:B) {
    # Draw n ROW INDICES WITH replacement, so entire rows are resampled
    idx <- sample.int(n, size = n, replace = TRUE)
    resample <- data[idx, , drop = FALSE]
    # Compute the statistic on this specific bootstrap sample
    boot_estimates[b] <- stat_fn(resample)
  }

  # Step 4: Extract SE and empirical percentile CI bounds
  se_boot <- sd(boot_estimates)
  alpha <- 1 - conf
  ci_lower <- quantile(boot_estimates, probs = alpha / 2, names = FALSE)
  ci_upper <- quantile(boot_estimates, probs = 1 - alpha / 2, names = FALSE)

  list(
    estimate  = theta_hat,
    se        = se_boot,
    ci        = c(lower = ci_lower, upper = ci_upper),
    conf      = conf,
    estimates = boot_estimates
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: data
nba <- read.csv(here("data", "basketball.csv"), sep = ";") |>
  filter(Competition == "NBA") |>
  select(Distance, Angle, Transition) |>
  na.omit()

stopifnot(all(nba$Transition %in% c(0, 1)))
```

```{r}
#| label: statistics

statistics <- list(
  mean = list(
    label = "Mean shot distance",
    fn    = function(d) mean(d$Distance)
  ),
  prop = list(
    label = "Proportion of transition shots",
    fn    = function(d) mean(d$Transition)
  ),
  cor = list(
    label = "Pearson correlation (angle, distance)",
    fn    = function(d) cor(d$Angle, d$Distance)
  ),
  dmed = list(
    label = "Difference in median distance (transition - non-transition)",
    fn    = function(d) median(d$Distance[d$Transition == 1]) -
                        median(d$Distance[d$Transition == 0])
  )
)
```


```{r}
#| label: estimation

B <- 2000

results <- lapply(seq_along(statistics), function(k) {
  fn <- statistics[[k]]$fn

  # Our implementation: percentile CI
  mine <- my_bootstrap(nba, stat_fn = fn, B = B, conf = 0.95, seed = 100 + k)

  # boot package: percentile and BCa CIs
  set.seed(100 + k)
  lib <- boot(data = nba, statistic = function(d, i) fn(d[i, , drop = FALSE]), R = B)
  ci  <- boot.ci(lib, conf = 0.95, type = c("perc", "bca"))

  list(mine = mine, lib = lib, perc = ci$percent[4:5], bca = ci$bca[4:5])
})
names(results) <- names(statistics)
labels <- sapply(statistics, `[[`, "label")

fmt <- function(x) sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", x[1], x[2])

comparison_table <- data.frame(
  Statistic  = unname(labels),
  Estimate   = sapply(results, function(r) r$mine$estimate),
  SE_ours    = sapply(results, function(r) r$mine$se),
  SE_boot    = sapply(results, function(r) sd(r$lib$t)),
  Perc_ours  = sapply(results, function(r) fmt(unname(r$mine$ci))),
  Perc_boot  = sapply(results, function(r) fmt(r$perc)),
  BCa_boot   = sapply(results, function(r) fmt(r$bca)),
  row.names  = NULL
)

# Point estimates, bootstrap SEs and 95% CIs (B = 2000) for NBA shots
#print(comparison_table, digits = 4)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-nba-bootstrap
#| fig-cap: "Bootstrap distributions (B = 2000, row resampling) of the 4 statistics for NBA shots. Dashed line: point estimate. Bars below histograms: 95% percentile CI from my_bootstrap() and 95% BCa CI from the boot package."

method_cols <- c("Percentile (my_bootstrap)" = "#0072B2",
                 "BCa (boot)"                = "#D55E00")

panel <- function(r, label) {
  est      <- r$mine$estimates
  dens_max <- max(density(est)$y)

  iv <- data.frame(
    method = factor(names(method_cols), levels = names(method_cols)),
    lo     = c(r$mine$ci[1], r$bca[1]),
    hi     = c(r$mine$ci[2], r$bca[2]),
    y      = -dens_max * c(0.10, 0.20)
  )

  ggplot() +
    geom_histogram(data = data.frame(est = est),
                   aes(x = est, y = after_stat(density)),
                   bins = 40, fill = "grey85", colour = "white") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = r$mine$estimate, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
    geom_segment(data = iv, aes(x = lo, xend = hi, y = y, yend = y, colour = method),
                 linewidth = 1.3) +
    geom_point(data = iv, aes(x = lo, y = y, colour = method), size = 1.8) +
    geom_point(data = iv, aes(x = hi, y = y, colour = method), size = 1.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = method_cols, name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.08))) +
    labs(
      title    = label,
      subtitle = sprintf("Estimate = %.3f, bootstrap SE = %.3f", r$mine$estimate, r$mine$se),
      x        = "Bootstrap estimate",
      y        = NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
      axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y  = element_blank(),
      plot.margin  = margin(t = 14, r = 8, b = 6, l = 26)  # prostor za črko panela
    )
}

panels <- Map(panel, results, labels)

fig <- (wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 2) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A",
                  theme = theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)))) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

fig
```
**Results.** Mean shot distance is 4.16 (SE 0.08), with a 95% CI of roughly 4.0 to 4.3. Transition shots make up 12.7% of NBA shots (SE 0.010; 95% CI about 10.9% to 14.6%). The correlation between shot angle and distance is 0.03 (SE 0.03); its CI covers zero, so there is no evidence of a linear association between the two. Transition shots are taken markedly closer to the basket: the difference in median distance is -2.88 (SE 0.48), and its CI (about -3.7 to -2.0) lies well below zero, so the difference is large compared with the sampling uncertainty. Percentile and BCa intervals lead to the same conclusions for all four statistics. Intervals are likely somewhat too narrow because shots from the same game or player are not independent, and the transition group is small (156 shots), which makes the median difference the least precise estimate.
